name: security-git-submodule-provenance-review
intent: Git submodule revision/source trust in a privileged build
artifacts: .gitmodules changes, recursive checkout options, pinned commits, URL rewriting and build consumer.
trace: Trace who can change the submodule URL/revision and whether the approved parent revision actually binds the bytes later built.
experiment: Use inert owned repositories and a local checkout; compare pinned intended content with an untrusted URL/ref update without running builds.
disproof: The presence of submodules is not a supply-chain flaw; approved immutable submodule content can be valid.
repair: Bind submodule source and revision to reviewed provenance, retesting recursive updates and approved release behavior.
branch_decisions: Bind .gitmodules URL changes, the committed gitlink SHA, recursive submodules and any update --remote behavior. A pinned SHA narrows content identity but does not prove an approved producer or safe build scripts. Rewriting a local URL is privileged fixture setup unless the protected build actually consumes an attacker-editable configuration source.
